decls.statement: def JDiff (s a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) : ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_def
decls.doc: The definition of `JDiff` as the expanded four-term formula.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_def (s a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s a t b =
      GridPoint.J s t - GridPoint.J s b - GridPoint.J a t + GridPoint.J a b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_comm
decls.doc: `JDiff` is symmetric in its two formal-difference inputs.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_comm (s a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s a t b = JDiff t b s a

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_self_left
decls.doc: The formal difference of a point set with itself has zero `J`-pairing on the left.
decls.statement: theorem JDiff_self_left (s t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) : JDiff s s t b = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_self_right
decls.doc: The formal difference of a point set with itself has zero `J`-pairing on the right.
decls.statement: theorem JDiff_self_right (s a t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) : JDiff s a t t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_left_sub_empty
decls.doc:
Pairing an ordinary point set with a formal difference is the corresponding difference of
two `J`-values.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_left_sub_empty (s t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s ∅ t b = GridPoint.J s t - GridPoint.J s b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_right_sub_empty
decls.doc:
Pairing a formal difference with an ordinary point set is the corresponding difference of
two `J`-values.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_right_sub_empty (s a t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s a t ∅ = GridPoint.J s t - GridPoint.J a t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_self_eq
decls.doc: The self-pairing of `s - a` expanded in symmetric form.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_self_eq (s a : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s a s a = GridPoint.J s s - 2 * GridPoint.J s a + GridPoint.J a a

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_self_eq_intCast
decls.doc:
The self-pairing `JDiff s a s a` is integer-valued: it is the cast of
`I(s, s) - JNum(s, a) + I(a, a)`. The two `J`-self-pairings are integers by `J_self`, and the
cross term `2 · J(s, a)` is the integer numerator `JNum(s, a)`, so every half cancels. This is the
general fact underlying the integer-valuedness of the Maslov gradings.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_self_eq_intCast (s a : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff s a s a = ((I s s : ℤ) - JNum s a + I a a : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_union_left
decls.doc: `JDiff` is additive in the left positive point set over disjoint unions.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_union_left {s₁ s₂ a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : Disjoint s₁ s₂) :
    JDiff (s₁ ∪ s₂) a t b =
      JDiff s₁ a t b + JDiff s₂ ∅ t b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_union_right
decls.doc: `JDiff` is additive in the right positive point set over disjoint unions.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_union_right {s a t₁ t₂ b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : Disjoint t₁ t₂) :
    JDiff s a (t₁ ∪ t₂) b =
      JDiff s a t₁ b + JDiff s a t₂ ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_singleton_singleton
decls.doc:
The numerator of `J` on singleton point sets records whether either point is southwest of
the other.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_singleton_singleton (p q : Fin n × Fin n) :
    JNum {p} {q} =
      (if IsSouthWest p q then 1 else 0) + (if IsSouthWest q p then 1 else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_singleton_singleton
decls.doc:
The `J`-function on singleton point sets is half the number of southwest comparisons
between the two points.
decls.statement:
theorem J_singleton_singleton (p q : Fin n × Fin n) :
    GridPoint.J {p} {q} =
      (((if IsSouthWest p q then 1 else 0) +
        (if IsSouthWest q p then 1 else 0) : ℕ) : ℚ) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_singleton_singleton_of_isSouthWest_or_isSouthWest
decls.doc: The `J`-function of two comparable singleton point sets is `1 / 2`.

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_singleton_self
decls.doc: The `J`-function of a singleton with itself is zero.
decls.statement: theorem J_singleton_self (p : Fin n × Fin n) : GridPoint.J {p} {p} = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_mono_left
decls.doc: The ordered southwest count is monotone in its left point set.
decls.statement:
theorem I_mono_left {s₁ s₂ t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) :
    I s₁ t ≤ I s₂ t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_mono_right
decls.doc: The ordered southwest count is monotone in its right point set.
decls.statement:
theorem I_mono_right {s t₁ t₂ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : t₁ ⊆ t₂) :
    I s t₁ ≤ I s t₂

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_mono_left
decls.doc: The numerator of `J` is monotone in its left point set.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_mono_left {s₁ s₂ t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) :
    JNum s₁ t ≤ JNum s₂ t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_mono_right
decls.doc: The numerator of `J` is monotone in its right point set.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_mono_right {s t₁ t₂ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)} (h : t₁ ⊆ t₂) :
    JNum s t₁ ≤ JNum s t₂

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.isSouthWest_swap
decls.doc:
The strict southwest relation is invariant under reflecting both points across the diagonal:
exchanging the column and row coordinates of both endpoints exchanges the two strict
inequalities.
decls.statement:
theorem isSouthWest_swap (p q : Fin n × Fin n) :
    IsSouthWest (Prod.swap p) (Prod.swap q) ↔ IsSouthWest p q

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.prodMap_swap_injective
decls.doc: The reflection map on pairs of grid squares is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap_swap_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (Prod.map (Prod.swap (α := Fin n) (β := Fin n)) (Prod.swap (α := Fin n) (β := Fin n)))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_image_swap
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count is invariant under reflecting both point sets across the
diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem I_image_swap (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    I (s.image Prod.swap) (t.image Prod.swap) = I s t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_image_swap
decls.doc:
The numerator of the `J`-function is invariant under reflecting both point sets across the
diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_image_swap (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JNum (s.image Prod.swap) (t.image Prod.swap) = JNum s t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_image_swap
decls.doc:
The symmetrized grid `J`-function is invariant under reflecting both point sets across the
diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem J_image_swap (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    GridPoint.J (s.image Prod.swap) (t.image Prod.swap) = GridPoint.J s t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_image_swap
decls.doc:
The bilinear `J`-function on formal differences is invariant under reflecting all four point
sets across the diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_image_swap (s a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff (s.image Prod.swap) (a.image Prod.swap) (t.image Prod.swap) (b.image Prod.swap)
      = JDiff s a t b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.isSouthWest_rev
decls.doc:
Reversing both coordinates of both points of a pair exchanges the two endpoints of the strict
southwest relation: it sends the column and row comparisons to their reverses.
decls.statement:
theorem isSouthWest_rev (p q : Fin n × Fin n) :
    IsSouthWest (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev p) (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev q) ↔ IsSouthWest q p

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.prodMap_rev_injective
decls.doc: The coordinate-reversal map on grid squares is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap_rev_injective :
    Function.Injective (Prod.map (Fin.rev (n := n)) (Fin.rev (n := n)))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.prodMap_prodMap_rev_injective
decls.doc: The coordinate-reversal map on pairs of grid squares is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap_prodMap_rev_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (Prod.map (Prod.map (Fin.rev (n := n)) (Fin.rev (n := n)))
        (Prod.map (Fin.rev (n := n)) (Fin.rev (n := n))))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_image_rev
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count is invariant, up to exchanging the two point sets, under reversing
both coordinates of both point sets. The reversal turns each southwest comparison into the
opposite comparison, so the count of southwest pairs from `s` to `t` becomes the count from `t`
to `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem I_image_rev (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    I (s.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) (t.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) = I t s

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_image_rev
decls.doc:
The numerator of the `J`-function is invariant under reversing both coordinates of both point
sets. The two ordered counts are exchanged by the reversal, and their sum is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_image_rev (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JNum (s.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) (t.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) = JNum s t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_image_rev
decls.doc:
The symmetrized grid `J`-function is invariant under reversing both coordinates of both point
sets.
decls.statement:
theorem J_image_rev (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    GridPoint.J (s.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) (t.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev))
      = GridPoint.J s t

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JDiff_image_rev
decls.doc:
The bilinear `J`-function on formal differences is invariant under reversing both coordinates
of all four point sets.
decls.statement:
theorem JDiff_image_rev (s a t b : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JDiff (s.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) (a.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev))
        (t.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)) (b.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev))
      = JDiff s a t b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_graph_eq_card
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count of two graph point sets is the number of column pairs `c < d`
where the source row precedes the target row. This graph-level statement does not require either
row assignment to be a permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem I_graph_eq_card (f g : Fin n → Fin n) :
    GridPoint.I (Finset.univ.image fun c : Fin n => (c, f c))
        (Finset.univ.image fun c : Fin n => (c, g c)) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ f p.1 < g p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J
decls.doc: The grid `J`-function applied to the point sets of two grid states.
decls.statement: def J (x y : GridState n) : ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J_def
decls.doc: The state-level grid `J`-function is the point-set `J`-function on state point sets.
decls.statement: theorem J_def (x y : GridState n) : GridState.J x y = GridPoint.J x.pointSet y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J_comm
decls.doc: The state-level grid `J`-function is symmetric.
decls.statement: theorem J_comm (x y : GridState n) : GridState.J x y = GridState.J y x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J_transpose
decls.doc:
The state-level grid `J`-function is invariant under reflecting both states across the
diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem J_transpose (x y : GridState n) :
    GridState.J x.transpose y.transpose = GridState.J x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J_rotate
decls.doc: The state-level grid `J`-function is invariant under the half-turn rotation of both states.
decls.statement:
theorem J_rotate (x y : GridState n) :
    GridState.J x.rotate y.rotate = GridState.J x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.I_pointSet_eq_card
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count of the point sets of two grid states is the number of column
pairs `c < d` at which the source row precedes the target row.
decls.statement:
theorem I_pointSet_eq_card (x y : GridState n) :
    GridPoint.I x.pointSet y.pointSet =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < y p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.JNum_pointSet_eq_card
decls.doc:
The symmetrized numerator of the grid `J`-function on two state point sets, as a sum of two
column-index counts.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_pointSet_eq_card (x y : GridState n) :
    GridPoint.JNum x.pointSet y.pointSet =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < y p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ y p.1 < x p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.J_pointSet_eq_card
decls.doc:
The rational grid `J`-function on two state point sets is half the sum of the two
column-index counts.
decls.statement:
theorem J_pointSet_eq_card (x y : GridState n) :
    GridState.J x y =
      (((Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < y p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ y p.1 < x p.2).card : ℕ) : ℚ)
        / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.I_self_pointSet_eq_card
decls.doc:
The self southwest count of a grid state is the number of *non-inversions* of its
permutation: column pairs `c < d` whose occupied rows are in the same order.
decls.statement:
theorem I_self_pointSet_eq_card (x : GridState n) :
    GridPoint.I x.pointSet x.pointSet =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < x p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card_filter_noninversion_add_card_filter_inversion
decls.doc:
The non-inversions and the inversions of a grid state partition the ordered column pairs: the
number of pairs `c < d` with `x c < x d` plus the number with `x d < x c` is the total number of
pairs `c < d`. The state's permutation is injective, so on each ordered column pair exactly one of
the two strict row comparisons holds.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_noninversion_add_card_filter_inversion (x : GridState n) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < x p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.2 < x p.1).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO
decls.doc: The grid `J`-function against the `O`-markings of a grid diagram.
decls.statement: def JO (x : GridState n) : ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_def
decls.doc: `JO` is the point-set `J`-function of a state against the `O`-markings.
decls.statement: theorem JO_def (x : GridState n) : GridDiagram.JO G x = GridPoint.J x.pointSet G.OSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX
decls.doc: The grid `J`-function against the `X`-markings of a grid diagram.
decls.statement: def JX (x : GridState n) : ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_def
decls.doc: `JX` is the point-set `J`-function of a state against the `X`-markings.
decls.statement: theorem JX_def (x : GridState n) : GridDiagram.JX G x = GridPoint.J x.pointSet G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_eq_card
decls.doc: The `O`-marking `J`-pairing as a column-index count.
decls.statement:
theorem JO_eq_card (x : GridState n) :
    G.JO x =
      (((Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < G.O p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ G.O p.1 < x p.2).card : ℕ) :
          ℚ) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_eq_card
decls.doc: The `X`-marking `J`-pairing as a column-index count.
decls.statement:
theorem JX_eq_card (x : GridState n) :
    G.JX x =
      (((Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < G.X p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ G.X p.1 < x p.2).card : ℕ) :
          ℚ) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_transpose
decls.doc: `JO` is invariant under reflecting the diagram and state across the diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem JO_transpose (x : GridState n) :
    GridDiagram.JO G.transpose x.transpose = GridDiagram.JO G x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_transpose
decls.doc: `JX` is invariant under reflecting the diagram and state across the diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem JX_transpose (x : GridState n) :
    GridDiagram.JX G.transpose x.transpose = GridDiagram.JX G x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_rotate
decls.doc: `JO` is invariant under the half-turn rotation of the diagram and state.
decls.statement:
theorem JO_rotate (x : GridState n) :
    GridDiagram.JO G.rotate x.rotate = GridDiagram.JO G x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_rotate
decls.doc: `JX` is invariant under the half-turn rotation of the diagram and state.
decls.statement:
theorem JX_rotate (x : GridState n) :
    GridDiagram.JX G.rotate x.rotate = GridDiagram.JX G x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_swapMarkings
decls.doc: The marking swap exchanges the `O`-marking `J`-pairing with the `X`-marking `J`-pairing.
decls.statement: theorem JO_swapMarkings (x : GridState n) : G.swapMarkings.JO x = G.JX x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_swapMarkings
decls.doc: The marking swap exchanges the `X`-marking `J`-pairing with the `O`-marking `J`-pairing.
decls.statement: theorem JX_swapMarkings (x : GridState n) : G.swapMarkings.JX x = G.JO x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JO_comm
decls.doc: `JO` may equivalently be read with the `O`-markings as the left input.
decls.statement: theorem JO_comm (x : GridState n) : GridDiagram.JO G x = GridPoint.J G.OSet x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.JX_comm
decls.doc: `JX` may equivalently be read with the `X`-markings as the left input.
decls.statement: theorem JX_comm (x : GridState n) : GridDiagram.JX G x = GridPoint.J G.XSet x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_eq_sum_card_filter
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count `I s t` is the sum, over the left points `p ∈ s`, of the number of
points of `t` strictly northeast of `p`.
decls.statement:
theorem I_eq_sum_card_filter (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    I s t = ∑ p ∈ s, (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_eq_sum_card_filter_right
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count `I s t` is the sum, over the right points `q ∈ t`, of the number of
points of `s` strictly southwest of `q`.
decls.statement:
theorem I_eq_sum_card_filter_right (s t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    I s t = ∑ q ∈ t, (s.filter fun p => IsSouthWest p q).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_singleton_left
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count of a single grid square against a point set `t` is the number of
points of `t` strictly northeast of it.
decls.statement:
theorem I_singleton_left (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    I {p} t = (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.I_singleton_right
decls.doc:
The ordered southwest count of a point set `s` against a single grid square is the number of
points of `s` strictly southwest of it.
decls.statement:
theorem I_singleton_right (s : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    I s {p} = (s.filter fun q => IsSouthWest q p).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_singleton_left
decls.doc:
The symmetrized numerator of the `J`-function against a single grid square splits into the two
directed counts: the points of `t` strictly northeast of the square and the points strictly
southwest of it.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_singleton_left (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JNum {p} t =
      (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q).card + (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest q p).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.disjoint_filter_isSouthWest
decls.doc:
No point of a set is both strictly northeast and strictly southwest of a fixed grid square, so
the two directed neighbor sets are disjoint.
decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_filter_isSouthWest (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    Disjoint (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q) (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest q p)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.JNum_singleton_left_eq_card
decls.doc:
The symmetrized numerator of the `J`-function against a single grid square is the number of
points of `t` strictly comparable to it: those either strictly northeast or strictly southwest. The
two directions never overlap, so the two counts combine into a single filter cardinality.
decls.statement:
theorem JNum_singleton_left_eq_card (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    JNum {p} t = (t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q ∨ IsSouthWest q p).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.J_singleton_left
decls.doc:
The `J`-pairing of a single grid square against a point set `t` is half the number of points of
`t` strictly comparable to it.
decls.statement:
theorem J_singleton_left (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    GridPoint.J {p} t =
      (((t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q ∨ IsSouthWest q p).card : ℕ) : ℚ) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridPoint.two_mul_J_singleton_left
decls.doc:
Twice the `J`-pairing of a single grid square against a point set `t` is the number of points
of `t` strictly comparable to it: in particular this pairing is a half-integer whose double is a
natural number.
decls.statement:
theorem two_mul_J_singleton_left (p : Fin n × Fin n) (t : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    2 * GridPoint.J {p} t = ((t.filter fun q => IsSouthWest p q ∨ IsSouthWest q p).card : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle
decls.doc:
A toroidal grid rectangle, represented by its oriented column and row sides.

The interior is the product of the clockwise open interval from `left` to `right` with the
clockwise open interval from `bottom` to `top`. Degenerate side choices are allowed at this
level; their interiors are empty in the degenerate direction.
decls.statement: structure GridRectangle (n : ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm
decls.doc:
The opposite toroidal rectangle, obtained by reversing the two vertical sides while
keeping the horizontal sides fixed.
decls.statement: def symm : GridRectangle n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm_left
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle's left side is the original right side.
decls.statement: theorem symm_left : R.symm.left = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm_right
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle's right side is the original left side.
decls.statement: theorem symm_right : R.symm.right = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm_bottom
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle has the same bottom row.
decls.statement: theorem symm_bottom : R.symm.bottom = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm_top
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle has the same top row.
decls.statement: theorem symm_top : R.symm.top = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.symm_symm
decls.doc: Reversing a toroidal rectangle twice gives the original rectangle.
decls.statement: theorem symm_symm : R.symm.symm = R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.columnInterior
decls.doc: The columns strictly inside a toroidal grid rectangle.
decls.statement: def columnInterior : Finset (Fin n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rowInterior
decls.doc: The rows strictly inside a toroidal grid rectangle.
decls.statement: def rowInterior : Finset (Fin n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_columnInterior
decls.doc:
Membership in the interior columns is membership in the corresponding open-open circular
interval.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_columnInterior (c : Fin n) :
    c ∈ R.columnInterior ↔ c ∈ Grid.cIoo R.left R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_rowInterior
decls.doc:
Membership in the interior rows is membership in the corresponding open-open circular
interval.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_rowInterior (r : Fin n) :
    r ∈ R.rowInterior ↔ r ∈ Grid.cIoo R.bottom R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.left_notMem_columnInterior
decls.doc: The left side is not an interior column.
decls.statement: theorem left_notMem_columnInterior : R.left ∉ R.columnInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.right_notMem_columnInterior
decls.doc: The right side is not an interior column.
decls.statement: theorem right_notMem_columnInterior : R.right ∉ R.columnInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.bottom_notMem_rowInterior
decls.doc: The bottom side is not an interior row.
decls.statement: theorem bottom_notMem_rowInterior : R.bottom ∉ R.rowInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.top_notMem_rowInterior
decls.doc: The top side is not an interior row.
decls.statement: theorem top_notMem_rowInterior : R.top ∉ R.rowInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior
decls.doc: The finite set of squares strictly inside a toroidal grid rectangle.
decls.statement: def interior : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_interior
decls.doc: Membership in a rectangle interior is membership in both one-dimensional open intervals.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_interior (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ R.interior ↔ p.1 ∈ R.columnInterior ∧ p.2 ∈ R.rowInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mk_mem_interior
decls.doc:
A coordinate pair lies in the rectangle interior exactly when its column and row lie in
the corresponding open cyclic intervals.
decls.statement:
theorem mk_mem_interior (c r : Fin n) :
    (c, r) ∈ R.interior ↔ c ∈ R.columnInterior ∧ r ∈ R.rowInterior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior_eq_empty_of_left_eq_right
decls.doc: A rectangle has empty interior if its two column sides coincide.
decls.statement: theorem interior_eq_empty_of_left_eq_right (h : R.left = R.right) : R.interior = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior_eq_empty_of_bottom_eq_top
decls.doc: A rectangle has empty interior if its two row sides coincide.
decls.statement: theorem interior_eq_empty_of_bottom_eq_top (h : R.bottom = R.top) : R.interior = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.card_interior
decls.doc:
The number of interior squares is the product of the numbers of interior columns and
interior rows.
decls.statement:
theorem card_interior :
    R.interior.card = R.columnInterior.card * R.rowInterior.card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior_eq_empty_of_le_two
decls.doc: In a grid of size at most two, every toroidal rectangle has empty interior.
decls.statement: theorem interior_eq_empty_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (R : GridRectangle n) : R.interior = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.IsEmptyFor
decls.doc: A rectangle is empty for a grid state when the state has no point in its interior.
decls.statement: def IsEmptyFor (x : GridState n) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.isEmptyFor_iff
decls.doc:
A rectangle is empty for a grid state exactly when no point of the state lies in its
interior.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmptyFor_iff (x : GridState n) :
    R.IsEmptyFor x ↔ ∀ p ∈ x.pointSet, p ∉ R.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.isEmptyFor_of_le_two
decls.doc: In a grid of size at most two, every toroidal rectangle is empty for every grid state.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmptyFor_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (R : GridRectangle n) (x : GridState n) :
    R.IsEmptyFor x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.AvoidsMarkings
decls.doc:
A rectangle avoids the markings of a grid diagram when its interior contains no `O` or
`X` marking.
decls.statement: def AvoidsMarkings (G : GridDiagram n) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.disjoint_interior_OSet_of_avoidsMarkings
decls.doc: A marking-avoiding rectangle has no `O` marking in its interior.
decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_interior_OSet_of_avoidsMarkings {G : GridDiagram n}
    (h : R.AvoidsMarkings G) : Disjoint R.interior G.OSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.disjoint_interior_XSet_of_avoidsMarkings
decls.doc: A marking-avoiding rectangle has no `X` marking in its interior.
decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_interior_XSet_of_avoidsMarkings {G : GridDiagram n}
    (h : R.AvoidsMarkings G) : Disjoint R.interior G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.avoidsMarkings_iff
decls.doc:
A rectangle avoids markings exactly when neither the `O` nor the `X` marking set meets
its interior.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_iff (G : GridDiagram n) :
    R.AvoidsMarkings G ↔
      Disjoint R.interior G.OSet ∧ Disjoint R.interior G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.avoidsMarkings_of_le_two
decls.doc: In a grid of size at most two, every toroidal rectangle avoids every diagram's markings.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (R : GridRectangle n) (G : GridDiagram n) :
    R.AvoidsMarkings G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.avoidsMarkings_swapMarkings
decls.doc:
Marking avoidance is unchanged by swapping the `O` and `X` markings, since it only refers to
the union of the two marking sets.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_swapMarkings (G : GridDiagram n) :
    R.AvoidsMarkings G.swapMarkings ↔ R.AvoidsMarkings G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose
decls.doc:
The diagonal reflection of a toroidal rectangle, exchanging the two vertical sides with the
two horizontal sides.

Reflecting across the main diagonal turns columns into rows and rows into columns, so the
interior is reflected by `Prod.swap`.
decls.statement: def transpose : GridRectangle n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose_left
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's left side is the original bottom side.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_left : R.transpose.left = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose_right
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's right side is the original top side.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_right : R.transpose.right = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose_bottom
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's bottom side is the original left side.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_bottom : R.transpose.bottom = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose_top
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's top side is the original right side.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_top : R.transpose.top = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.transpose_transpose
decls.doc: Reflecting a toroidal rectangle twice gives the original rectangle.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_transpose : R.transpose.transpose = R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior_transpose
decls.doc:
The interior of the reflected rectangle is the diagonal reflection of the original
interior.
decls.statement: theorem interior_transpose : R.transpose.interior = R.interior.image Prod.swap

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rotate
decls.doc:
The half-turn rotation of a toroidal rectangle.

Reversing both coordinates reverses the cyclic order in each direction, so the two vertical sides
are reversed and exchanged, and likewise the two horizontal sides.
decls.statement: def rotate : GridRectangle n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rotate_left
decls.doc: The rotated rectangle's left side is the reversed original right side.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_left : R.rotate.left = R.right.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rotate_right
decls.doc: The rotated rectangle's right side is the reversed original left side.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_right : R.rotate.right = R.left.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rotate_bottom
decls.doc: The rotated rectangle's bottom side is the reversed original top side.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_bottom : R.rotate.bottom = R.top.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rotate_top
decls.doc: The rotated rectangle's top side is the reversed original bottom side.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_top : R.rotate.top = R.bottom.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.columnInterior_rotate
decls.doc: The interior columns of the rotated rectangle are the reversed original interior columns.
decls.statement: theorem columnInterior_rotate : R.rotate.columnInterior = R.columnInterior.image Fin.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.rowInterior_rotate
decls.doc: The interior rows of the rotated rectangle are the reversed original interior rows.
decls.statement: theorem rowInterior_rotate : R.rotate.rowInterior = R.rowInterior.image Fin.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.interior_rotate
decls.doc: The interior of the rotated rectangle is the half-turn rotation of the original interior.
decls.statement:
theorem interior_rotate :
    R.rotate.interior = R.interior.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween
decls.doc:
An oriented toroidal rectangle from one grid state to another.

The two states agree outside the two side columns, and in those side columns they exchange the
two rows. Swapping `left` and `right` gives the complementary oriented rectangle.
decls.statement: structure GridRectangleBetween {n : ℕ} (x y : GridState n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.sidePair_injective
decls.doc: A rectangle between two grid states is determined by its two side columns.
decls.statement:
theorem sidePair_injective :
    Function.Injective fun R : GridRectangleBetween x y => (R.left, R.right)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.instDecidableEq
decls.doc:
An oriented rectangle between two grid states has decidable equality: it is determined by its
ordered pair of side columns, which has decidable equality.
decls.statement: instance : DecidableEq (GridRectangleBetween x y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.instFintype
decls.doc:
For fixed source and target grid states, the oriented rectangles between them form a
finite type. Each rectangle is determined by its two side columns.
decls.statement: instance : Fintype (GridRectangleBetween x y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.all
decls.doc: The finite set of all oriented rectangles from `x` to `y`.
decls.statement: def all (x y : GridState n) : Finset (GridRectangleBetween x y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.mem_all
decls.doc: Membership in `GridRectangleBetween.all` is automatic.
decls.statement: theorem mem_all (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R ∈ all x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.bottom
decls.doc: The row of `x` on the initial side.
decls.statement: def bottom : Fin n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.top
decls.doc: The row of `x` on the terminal side.
decls.statement: def top : Fin n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.toGridRectangle
decls.doc: The associated toroidal rectangle.
decls.statement: def toGridRectangle : GridRectangle n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm
decls.doc:
The opposite oriented rectangle, obtained by reversing the two side columns.

If `R` goes from `x` to `y`, then `R.symm` goes from `y` back to `x`. It has the same two
horizontal side rows and traverses the complementary horizontal direction on the torus.
decls.statement: def symm (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : GridRectangleBetween y x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_left
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle's left side is the original right side.
decls.statement: theorem symm_left (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.symm.left = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_right
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle's right side is the original left side.
decls.statement: theorem symm_right (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.symm.right = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_symm
decls.doc: Reversing an oriented rectangle twice gives the original rectangle.
decls.statement: theorem symm_symm (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.symm.symm = R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_inj
decls.doc: Reversal is injective on oriented rectangles.
decls.statement: theorem symm_inj {R S : GridRectangleBetween x y} : R.symm = S.symm ↔ R = S

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symmEquiv
decls.doc:
Opposite rectangles give an equivalence between rectangles from `x` to `y` and from `y`
to `x`.
decls.statement: def symmEquiv (x y : GridState n) : GridRectangleBetween x y ≃ GridRectangleBetween y x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symmEquiv_apply
decls.doc: Applying the opposite-rectangle equivalence is `GridRectangleBetween.symm`.
decls.statement:
theorem symmEquiv_apply (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    symmEquiv x y R = R.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symmEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: Applying the inverse opposite-rectangle equivalence is `GridRectangleBetween.symm`.
decls.statement:
theorem symmEquiv_symm_apply (R : GridRectangleBetween y x) :
    (symmEquiv x y).symm R = R.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_bottom
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle has the same bottom row.
decls.statement: theorem symm_bottom (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.symm.bottom = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_top
decls.doc: The opposite rectangle has the same top row.
decls.statement: theorem symm_top (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.symm.top = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_toGridRectangle
decls.doc:
The associated toroidal rectangle of the opposite oriented rectangle is the opposite of
the associated toroidal rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem symm_toGridRectangle (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.symm.toGridRectangle = R.toGridRectangle.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.bottom_ne_top
decls.doc: The two side rows of a rectangle between states are distinct.
decls.statement: theorem bottom_ne_top : R.bottom ≠ R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.source_ne_target
decls.doc:
A rectangle between grid states has distinct source and target states. A self-rectangle
would force the source state's permutation to take the same value on the two distinct side
columns.
decls.statement: theorem source_ne_target (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : x ≠ y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.all_self
decls.doc: There are no rectangles from a grid state to itself.
decls.statement: theorem all_self (x : GridState n) : all x x = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.left_bottom_mem_source
decls.doc: The initial lower corner is a point of the source state.
decls.statement: theorem left_bottom_mem_source : (R.left, R.bottom) ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.right_top_mem_source
decls.doc: The terminal upper corner is a point of the source state.
decls.statement: theorem right_top_mem_source : (R.right, R.top) ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.left_top_mem_target
decls.doc: The initial upper corner is a point of the target state.
decls.statement: theorem left_top_mem_target : (R.left, R.top) ∈ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.right_bottom_mem_target
decls.doc: The terminal lower corner is a point of the target state.
decls.statement: theorem right_bottom_mem_target : (R.right, R.bottom) ∈ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_left_bottom_mem_source
decls.doc:
The lower-left corner of the opposite rectangle is a target-state point of the original
rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem symm_left_bottom_mem_source (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    (R.symm.left, R.symm.bottom) ∈ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_right_top_mem_source
decls.doc:
The upper-right corner of the opposite rectangle is a target-state point of the original
rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem symm_right_top_mem_source (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    (R.symm.right, R.symm.top) ∈ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_left_top_mem_target
decls.doc:
The upper-left corner of the opposite rectangle is a source-state point of the original
rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem symm_left_top_mem_target (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    (R.symm.left, R.symm.top) ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.symm_right_bottom_mem_target
decls.doc:
The lower-right corner of the opposite rectangle is a source-state point of the original
rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem symm_right_bottom_mem_target (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    (R.symm.right, R.symm.bottom) ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_all_comm
decls.doc: There are as many oriented rectangles from `x` to `y` as from `y` to `x`.
decls.statement: theorem card_all_comm (x y : GridState n) : (all x y).card = (all y x).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.mem_target_pointSet_iff_of_ne
decls.doc: Away from the two side columns, membership in the source and target states is identical.

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.IsEmpty
decls.doc:
The associated rectangle is empty for the source state when no source-state point lies in
its interior.
decls.statement: def IsEmpty : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.emptyRectangles
decls.doc: The finite set of empty oriented rectangles from `x` to `y`.
decls.statement: def emptyRectangles (x y : GridState n) : Finset (GridRectangleBetween x y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.mem_emptyRectangles
decls.doc: Membership in the finite set of empty rectangles is exactly the emptiness predicate.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_emptyRectangles (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R ∈ emptyRectangles x y ↔ R.IsEmpty

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_of_mem_emptyRectangles
decls.doc: Every rectangle in `emptyRectangles` is empty.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_of_mem_emptyRectangles {R : GridRectangleBetween x y}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_of_le_two
decls.doc: In grid size at most two, every oriented rectangle between grid states is empty.
decls.statement: theorem isEmpty_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.IsEmpty

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.emptyRectangles_subset_all
decls.doc: Empty rectangles are a subset of all rectangles between the same two states.
decls.statement:
theorem emptyRectangles_subset_all (x y : GridState n) :
    emptyRectangles x y ⊆ all x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.emptyRectangles_eq_all_of_le_two
decls.doc: In grid size at most two, the empty rectangles are all oriented rectangles.
decls.statement:
theorem emptyRectangles_eq_all_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (x y : GridState n) :
    emptyRectangles x y = all x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.emptyRectangles_self
decls.doc: There are no empty rectangles from a grid state to itself.
decls.statement: theorem emptyRectangles_self (x : GridState n) : emptyRectangles x x = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.AvoidsMarkings
decls.doc:
The associated rectangle avoids a grid diagram's markings when no marking lies in its
interior.
decls.statement: def AvoidsMarkings (G : GridDiagram n) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.not_mem_interior_of_isEmpty
decls.doc: The source state has no point in the interior of an empty rectangle between states.
decls.statement:
theorem not_mem_interior_of_isEmpty (h : R.IsEmpty) {p : Fin n × Fin n}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_iff
decls.doc:
A rectangle between states is empty exactly when no source-state point lies in its
interior.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_iff :
    R.IsEmpty ↔ ∀ p ∈ x.pointSet, p ∉ R.toGridRectangle.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.not_mem_interior_of_fst_eq_left
decls.doc:
If a target-state point lies on a side column, then it is not in the associated
rectangle's interior.
decls.statement:
theorem not_mem_interior_of_fst_eq_left {p : Fin n × Fin n} (hp : p.1 = R.left) :
    p ∉ R.toGridRectangle.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.not_mem_interior_of_fst_eq_right
decls.doc:
If a target-state point lies on the other side column, then it is not in the associated
rectangle's interior.
decls.statement:
theorem not_mem_interior_of_fst_eq_right {p : Fin n × Fin n} (hp : p.1 = R.right) :
    p ∉ R.toGridRectangle.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_iff_target
decls.doc:
A rectangle between states is empty exactly when no target-state point lies in its
interior.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_iff_target :
    R.IsEmpty ↔ ∀ p ∈ y.pointSet, p ∉ R.toGridRectangle.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.not_mem_interior_target_of_isEmpty
decls.doc: The target state has no point in the interior of an empty rectangle between states.
decls.statement:
theorem not_mem_interior_target_of_isEmpty (h : R.IsEmpty) {p : Fin n × Fin n}
    (hp : p ∈ y.pointSet) : p ∉ R.toGridRectangle.interior

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.avoidsMarkings_iff
decls.doc:
A rectangle between states avoids markings exactly when neither marking set meets its
interior.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_iff (G : GridDiagram n) :
    R.AvoidsMarkings G ↔
      Disjoint R.toGridRectangle.interior G.OSet ∧
        Disjoint R.toGridRectangle.interior G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.disjoint_interior_OSet_of_avoidsMarkings
decls.doc: A marking-avoiding rectangle between states has no `O` marking in its interior.
decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_interior_OSet_of_avoidsMarkings {G : GridDiagram n}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.disjoint_interior_XSet_of_avoidsMarkings
