decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_interior_XSet_of_avoidsMarkings {G : GridDiagram n}
    (h : R.AvoidsMarkings G) : Disjoint R.toGridRectangle.interior G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose
decls.doc:
The diagonal reflection of an oriented rectangle from `x` to `y`, an oriented rectangle from
`x.transpose` to `y.transpose`.

Reflecting across the main diagonal exchanges the side columns with the side rows: the new side
columns are the two rows `x R.left` and `x R.right` that `R` connects.
decls.statement:
def transpose (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    GridRectangleBetween x.transpose y.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_left
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's initial side column is the original initial side row.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_left (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.transpose.left = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_right
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's terminal side column is the original terminal side row.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_right (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.transpose.right = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_bottom
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's initial side row is the original initial side column.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_bottom (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.transpose.bottom = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_top
decls.doc: The reflected rectangle's terminal side row is the original terminal side column.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_top (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.transpose.top = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_toGridRectangle
decls.doc: The toroidal rectangle of the reflected oriented rectangle, written out by its four sides.

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.eq_of_sides
decls.doc: Two oriented rectangles between the same states with equal side columns are equal.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_of_sides {R S : GridRectangleBetween x y} (hleft : R.left = S.left)
    (hright : R.right = S.right) : R = S

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides
decls.doc:
The oriented rectangle from `x` to `y` obtained by exchanging the two side columns.

It connects the same two states `x` and `y` -- the two states still exchange rows at the two
side columns and agree elsewhere -- but traverses the complementary toroidal region. This is not
the opposite rectangle `symm`, which runs from `y` back to `x`.
decls.statement: def swapSides (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : GridRectangleBetween x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_left_aux
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_left_aux (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.left = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_right_aux
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_right_aux (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.right = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_bottom_aux
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_bottom_aux (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.bottom = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_top_aux
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_top_aux (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.top = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_toGridRectangle_aux
TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_left
decls.doc: The side-swapped rectangle's initial side column is the original terminal side column.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_left (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.left = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_right
decls.doc: The side-swapped rectangle's terminal side column is the original initial side column.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_right (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.right = R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_bottom
decls.doc: The side-swapped rectangle's bottom row is the original top row.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_bottom (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.bottom = R.top

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_top
decls.doc: The side-swapped rectangle's top row is the original bottom row.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_top (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.top = R.bottom

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_toGridRectangle
decls.doc:
The toroidal rectangle of the side-swapped oriented rectangle, written out by its four
sides.

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_swapSides
decls.doc: Exchanging the two side columns twice gives the original rectangle.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_swapSides (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides.swapSides = R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.swapSides_ne_self
decls.doc:
Exchanging the two side columns gives a genuinely different rectangle, since the two side
columns are distinct.
decls.statement: theorem swapSides_ne_self (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.swapSides ≠ R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_transpose
decls.doc: Reflecting an oriented rectangle twice gives the original rectangle.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_transpose (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.transpose.transpose = R

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transposeEquiv
decls.doc:
The diagonal reflection as an equivalence between oriented rectangles from `x` to `y` and
oriented rectangles from `x.transpose` to `y.transpose`. Since reflecting twice is the identity,
`transpose` is its own inverse.
decls.statement:
def transposeEquiv (x y : GridState n) :
    GridRectangleBetween x y ≃ GridRectangleBetween x.transpose y.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transposeEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The transpose equivalence applies a rectangle by reflecting it.
decls.statement:
theorem transposeEquiv_apply (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    transposeEquiv x y R = R.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transposeEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse of the transpose equivalence is again reflection.
decls.statement:
theorem transposeEquiv_symm_apply (R : GridRectangleBetween x.transpose y.transpose) :
    (transposeEquiv x y).symm R = R.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_injective
decls.doc: The diagonal reflection is injective on oriented rectangles.
decls.statement:
theorem transpose_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (transpose : GridRectangleBetween x y → GridRectangleBetween x.transpose y.transpose)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.transpose_inj
decls.doc: Two oriented rectangles have equal diagonal reflections exactly when they are equal.
decls.statement:
theorem transpose_inj {R S : GridRectangleBetween x y} :
    R.transpose = S.transpose ↔ R = S

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.interior_transpose
decls.doc:
The interior of the reflected rectangle is the diagonal reflection of the interior of the
original rectangle. This is the oriented-rectangle corollary of
`GridRectangle.interior_transpose`.
decls.statement:
theorem interior_transpose (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.transpose.toGridRectangle.interior = R.toGridRectangle.interior.image Prod.swap

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_transpose
decls.doc: The diagonal reflection preserves emptiness of a rectangle between grid states.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_transpose (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.transpose.IsEmpty ↔ R.IsEmpty

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.avoidsMarkings_transpose
decls.doc: The diagonal reflection preserves marking avoidance of a rectangle between grid states.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_transpose (G : GridDiagram n) (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.transpose.AvoidsMarkings G.transpose ↔ R.AvoidsMarkings G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.avoidsMarkings_swapMarkings
decls.doc:
Swapping the `O` and `X` markings preserves marking avoidance of a rectangle between grid
states.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_swapMarkings (G : GridDiagram n) (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.AvoidsMarkings G.swapMarkings ↔ R.AvoidsMarkings G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate
decls.doc:
The half-turn rotation of an oriented rectangle from `x` to `y`, an oriented rectangle from
`x.rotate` to `y.rotate`.

Reversing both coordinates reverses and exchanges the two side columns: the new initial side is
the reversed terminal column `R.rightᵒ` and the new terminal side is the reversed initial column
`R.leftᵒ`.
decls.statement: def rotate (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate_left
decls.doc: The rotated oriented rectangle's initial side column is the reversed terminal side column.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_left (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.rotate.left = R.right.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate_right
decls.doc: The rotated oriented rectangle's terminal side column is the reversed initial side column.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_right (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.rotate.right = R.left.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate_bottom
decls.doc: The rotated oriented rectangle's initial side row is the reversed terminal side row.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_bottom (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.rotate.bottom = R.top.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate_top
decls.doc: The rotated oriented rectangle's terminal side row is the reversed initial side row.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_top (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) : R.rotate.top = R.bottom.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotate_toGridRectangle
decls.doc:
The toroidal rectangle of the rotated oriented rectangle is the rotation of the toroidal
rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem rotate_toGridRectangle (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.rotate.toGridRectangle = R.toGridRectangle.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.interior_rotate
decls.doc:
The interior of the rotated oriented rectangle is the half-turn rotation of the interior of
the original oriented rectangle.
decls.statement:
theorem interior_rotate (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.rotate.toGridRectangle.interior =
      R.toGridRectangle.interior.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateSymm
decls.doc:
The inverse half-turn rotation, an oriented rectangle from `x` to `y` built from one between
the rotated states. It reverses and exchanges the side columns by the same recipe as `rotate`,
but lands in `GridRectangleBetween x y` directly; reversal is only an involution up to
`Fin.rev_rev`, so this avoids transporting along the (non-definitional) state involution.
decls.statement: def rotateSymm (S : GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate) : GridRectangleBetween x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateSymm_left
decls.doc: The inverse rotation's initial side column is the reversed terminal side column.
decls.statement:
theorem rotateSymm_left (S : GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate) :
    (rotateSymm S).left = S.right.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateSymm_right
decls.doc: The inverse rotation's terminal side column is the reversed initial side column.
decls.statement:
theorem rotateSymm_right (S : GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate) :
    (rotateSymm S).right = S.left.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateEquiv
decls.doc:
The half-turn rotation as an equivalence between oriented rectangles from `x` to `y` and
oriented rectangles from `x.rotate` to `y.rotate`.
decls.statement:
def rotateEquiv (x y : GridState n) :
    GridRectangleBetween x y ≃ GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The rotation equivalence applies a rectangle by rotating it.
decls.statement:
theorem rotateEquiv_apply (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    rotateEquiv x y R = R.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.rotateEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse of the rotation equivalence is the inverse rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem rotateEquiv_symm_apply (S : GridRectangleBetween x.rotate y.rotate) :
    (rotateEquiv x y).symm S = rotateSymm S

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.isEmpty_rotate
decls.doc: The half-turn rotation preserves emptiness of a rectangle between grid states.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_rotate (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.rotate.IsEmpty ↔ R.IsEmpty

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.avoidsMarkings_rotate
decls.doc: The half-turn rotation preserves marking avoidance of a rectangle between grid states.
decls.statement:
theorem avoidsMarkings_rotate (G : GridDiagram n) (R : GridRectangleBetween x y) :
    R.rotate.AvoidsMarkings G.rotate ↔ R.AvoidsMarkings G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.apply_ne_iff
decls.doc:
A column is a side column of the rectangle exactly when the two states read different rows
there. Away from the two side columns the states agree, and at a side column the source
permutation is injective on the two distinct side columns, so the read rows differ.
decls.statement: theorem apply_ne_iff (c : Fin n) : y c ≠ x c ↔ c = R.left ∨ c = R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.left_apply_ne
decls.doc: The states differ at the initial side column.
decls.statement: theorem left_apply_ne : y R.left ≠ x R.left

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.right_apply_ne
decls.doc: The states differ at the terminal side column.
decls.statement: theorem right_apply_ne : y R.right ≠ x R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.eq_or_eq_swapSides
decls.doc:
Any oriented rectangle between the same two states is `R` or its side swap `R.swapSides`. Its
two side columns are exactly the two columns where `x` and `y` differ, which are `R.left` and
`R.right`, so its ordered side pair is one of the two orderings of that pair.
decls.statement: theorem eq_or_eq_swapSides (S : GridRectangleBetween x y) : S = R ∨ S = R.swapSides

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.all_subset_pair
decls.doc: The oriented rectangles between two states are contained in the pair `{R, R.swapSides}`.
decls.statement: theorem all_subset_pair : all x y ⊆ {R, R.swapSides}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.all_eq_pair
decls.doc:
Given one oriented rectangle between two states, the oriented rectangles between them are
exactly the pair `{R, R.swapSides}`.
decls.statement: theorem all_eq_pair : all x y = {R, R.swapSides}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_all_le_two
decls.doc: There are at most two oriented rectangles between two grid states.
decls.statement: theorem card_all_le_two (x y : GridState n) : (all x y).card ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_all_eq_two_of_nonempty
decls.doc:
When there is at least one oriented rectangle between two states, there are exactly two: the
chosen one and its side swap.
decls.statement: theorem card_all_eq_two_of_nonempty (h : (all x y).Nonempty) : (all x y).card = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_le_two
decls.doc:
Any finite subcollection of oriented rectangles between two states has cardinality at most
two.
decls.statement: theorem card_le_two (s : Finset (GridRectangleBetween x y)) : s.card ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_emptyRectangles_le_two
decls.doc: There are at most two empty oriented rectangles between two grid states.
decls.statement:
theorem card_emptyRectangles_le_two (x y : GridState n) :
    (emptyRectangles x y).card ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.target_apply
decls.doc:
Pointwise form of the column-transposition identity: at each column the target state reads
the row the source state reads at the swapped column.
decls.statement: theorem target_apply (c : Fin n) : y c = x (Equiv.swap R.left R.right c)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.target_eq_swapColumns
decls.doc:
The target state of an oriented rectangle is the source state with its two side columns
swapped. The rectangle's defining equations -- the two side columns exchange their rows and the
other columns are unchanged -- are precisely the action of the column transposition.
decls.statement: theorem target_eq_swapColumns : y = x.swapColumns R.left R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.nonempty_all_iff
decls.doc:
Oriented rectangles between `x` and `y` exist exactly when `y` is a column transposition of
`x`. A rectangle realizes its side columns as a transposition taking `x` to `y`, and conversely a
column transposition exhibits an oriented rectangle on those two columns.
decls.statement:
theorem nonempty_all_iff :
    (all x y).Nonempty ↔ ∃ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b ∧ y = x.swapColumns a b

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.source_eq_swapColumns
decls.doc:
The source state of an oriented rectangle is the target state with its two side columns
swapped: swapping the same pair of columns twice is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem source_eq_swapColumns : x = y.swapColumns R.left R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.target_toPerm_eq
decls.doc:
The underlying permutation of the target state is the source permutation precomposed with
the transposition of the two side columns.
decls.statement:
theorem target_toPerm_eq :
    y.toPerm = (Equiv.swap R.left R.right).trans x.toPerm

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.mem_target_pointSet_iff
decls.doc:
A square lies in the target state exactly when its column-transposed square lies in the
source state.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_target_pointSet_iff (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ y.pointSet ↔ (Equiv.swap R.left R.right p.1, p.2) ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.mem_pointSet_inter_iff
decls.doc:
The two side columns carry the four corners of a rectangle, so a square that the two states
share must avoid both side columns. Conversely, away from the side columns the two states agree,
so every source square off the side columns is shared.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_pointSet_inter_iff (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet ↔
      p ∈ x.pointSet ∧ p.1 ≠ R.left ∧ p.1 ≠ R.right

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.left_bottom_notMem_inter
decls.doc: The lower-left corner is not shared with the target state: it sits on a side column.
decls.statement:
theorem left_bottom_notMem_inter :
    (R.left, R.bottom) ∉ x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.right_top_notMem_inter
decls.doc: The upper-right corner is not shared with the target state: it sits on a side column.
decls.statement:
theorem right_top_notMem_inter :
    (R.right, R.top) ∉ x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.left_top_notMem_inter
decls.doc: The upper-left target corner is not shared with the source state: it sits on a side column.
decls.statement:
theorem left_top_notMem_inter :
    (R.left, R.top) ∉ x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.right_bottom_notMem_inter
decls.doc: The lower-right target corner is not shared with the source state: it sits on a side column.
decls.statement:
theorem right_bottom_notMem_inter :
    (R.right, R.bottom) ∉ x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.source_pointSet_eq
decls.doc:
The source state's point set is its shared intersection with the target point set together
with the two source corners `(R.left, R.bottom)` and `(R.right, R.top)`.
decls.statement:
theorem source_pointSet_eq :
    x.pointSet =
      insert (R.left, R.bottom) (insert (R.right, R.top) (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.target_pointSet_eq
decls.doc: The target state's point set is the shared part together with its own two corners.
decls.statement:
theorem target_pointSet_eq :
    y.pointSet =
      insert (R.left, R.top) (insert (R.right, R.bottom) (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridRectangleBetween.card_pointSet_inter
decls.doc:
The source and target states share exactly `n - 2` squares: all of the source's `n` squares
except its two corners.
decls.statement: theorem card_pointSet_inter : (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet).card = n - 2

decls.name: TauCeti.rev2_rev2
decls.doc: Reversing both coordinates of a grid square twice returns the original square.
decls.statement:
theorem rev2_rev2 (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev p) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.revPerm_trans_swap_trans_revPerm
decls.doc: Conjugating a row or column swap by coordinate reversal swaps the reversed indices.
decls.statement:
theorem revPerm_trans_swap_trans_revPerm (a b : Fin n) :
    Fin.revPerm.trans ((Equiv.swap a b).trans Fin.revPerm) = Equiv.swap a.rev b.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.rotate
decls.doc:
The half-turn rotation of a grid state.

Rotating the occupied squares by `180°` reverses both the column and the row coordinate. It is
the composition of the column and row relabelings by the coordinate reversal `Fin.revPerm`.
decls.statement: def rotate (x : GridState n) : GridState n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.rotate_apply
decls.doc:
The rotated state reads off a column by reversing it, applying the original state, and
reversing the resulting row.
decls.statement:
theorem rotate_apply (x : GridState n) (c : Fin n) :
    x.rotate c = (x (Fin.rev c)).rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.columnOfRow_rotate
decls.doc:
In the rotated state, the occupied square in row `r` lies in the reversed column of the
occupied square in row `r.rev` of the original state.
decls.statement:
theorem columnOfRow_rotate (x : GridState n) (r : Fin n) :
    x.rotate.columnOfRow r = (x.columnOfRow r.rev).rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.mem_pointSet_rotate
decls.doc:
A square lies in the rotated state exactly when its half-turn rotation lies in the original
state.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_pointSet_rotate (x : GridState n) (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ x.rotate.pointSet ↔ Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev p ∈ x.pointSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.rotate_pointSet
decls.doc: The point set of the rotated state is the half-turn rotation of the original point set.
decls.statement:
theorem rotate_pointSet (x : GridState n) :
    x.rotate.pointSet = x.pointSet.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.rotate_rotate
decls.doc: The half-turn rotation is an involution on grid states.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_rotate (x : GridState n) : x.rotate.rotate = x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.transpose_rotate
decls.doc: Diagonal reflection commutes with the half-turn rotation of a grid state.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_rotate (x : GridState n) : x.transpose.rotate = x.rotate.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.relabelRows_rotate
decls.doc:
Row relabeling before rotation becomes row relabeling by the conjugate permutation after
rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelRows_rotate (ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (x : GridState n) :
    (x.relabelRows ρ).rotate = x.rotate.relabelRows (Fin.revPerm.trans (ρ.trans Fin.revPerm))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.relabelColumns_rotate
decls.doc:
Column relabeling before rotation becomes column relabeling by the conjugate permutation
after rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelColumns_rotate (κ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (x : GridState n) :
    (x.relabelColumns κ).rotate =
      x.rotate.relabelColumns (Fin.revPerm.trans (κ.trans Fin.revPerm))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.swapRows_rotate
decls.doc: Swapping rows before rotation is the same as swapping the reversed rows after rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem swapRows_rotate (a b : Fin n) (x : GridState n) :
    (x.swapRows a b).rotate = x.rotate.swapRows a.rev b.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.swapColumns_rotate
decls.doc:
Swapping columns before rotation is the same as swapping the reversed columns after
rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem swapColumns_rotate (a b : Fin n) (x : GridState n) :
    (x.swapColumns a b).rotate = x.rotate.swapColumns a.rev b.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate
decls.doc:
The half-turn rotation of a grid diagram, rotating both marking states.

It is the composition of the column and row relabelings by the coordinate reversal `Fin.revPerm`,
applied to both marking states at once. Each relabeling is again a grid diagram, so rotation
preserves the condition that no square carries both an `O` and an `X` marking.
decls.statement: def rotate (G : GridDiagram n) : GridDiagram n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate_O
decls.doc: The `O`-marking state of the rotated diagram is the rotation of the original `O`-state.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_O : G.rotate.O = G.O.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate_X
decls.doc: The `X`-marking state of the rotated diagram is the rotation of the original `X`-state.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_X : G.rotate.X = G.X.rotate

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.OColumnOfRow_rotate
decls.doc:
In the rotated diagram, the `O` marking in row `r` lies in the reversed column of the
original `O` marking in row `r.rev`.
decls.statement:
theorem OColumnOfRow_rotate (r : Fin n) :
    OColumnOfRow G.rotate r = (OColumnOfRow G r.rev).rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.XColumnOfRow_rotate
decls.doc:
In the rotated diagram, the `X` marking in row `r` lies in the reversed column of the
original `X` marking in row `r.rev`.
decls.statement:
theorem XColumnOfRow_rotate (r : Fin n) :
    XColumnOfRow G.rotate r = (XColumnOfRow G r.rev).rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate_OSet
decls.doc:
The `O`-markings of the rotated diagram are the half-turn rotation of the original
`O`-markings.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_OSet : G.rotate.OSet = G.OSet.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate_XSet
decls.doc:
The `X`-markings of the rotated diagram are the half-turn rotation of the original
`X`-markings.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_XSet : G.rotate.XSet = G.XSet.image (Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.mem_OSet_rotate
decls.doc:
A square lies in the rotated diagram's `O`-marking set exactly when its half-turn rotation
lies in the original `O`-marking set.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_OSet_rotate (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ G.rotate.OSet ↔ Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev p ∈ G.OSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.mem_XSet_rotate
decls.doc:
A square lies in the rotated diagram's `X`-marking set exactly when its half-turn rotation
lies in the original `X`-marking set.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_XSet_rotate (p : Fin n × Fin n) :
    p ∈ G.rotate.XSet ↔ Prod.map Fin.rev Fin.rev p ∈ G.XSet

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.rotate_rotate
decls.doc: The half-turn rotation is an involution on grid diagrams.
decls.statement: theorem rotate_rotate : G.rotate.rotate = G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.transpose_rotate
decls.doc: Diagonal reflection commutes with the half-turn rotation of a grid diagram.
decls.statement: theorem transpose_rotate : G.transpose.rotate = G.rotate.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.relabelRows_rotate
decls.doc:
Row relabeling before rotation becomes row relabeling by the conjugate permutation after
rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelRows_rotate (ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (G.relabelRows ρ).rotate = G.rotate.relabelRows (Fin.revPerm.trans (ρ.trans Fin.revPerm))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.relabelColumns_rotate
decls.doc:
Column relabeling before rotation becomes column relabeling by the conjugate permutation
after rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelColumns_rotate (κ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (G.relabelColumns κ).rotate =
      G.rotate.relabelColumns (Fin.revPerm.trans (κ.trans Fin.revPerm))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.swapRows_rotate
decls.doc: Swapping rows before rotation is the same as swapping the reversed rows after rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem swapRows_rotate (a b : Fin n) :
    (G.swapRows a b).rotate = G.rotate.swapRows a.rev b.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.swapColumns_rotate
decls.doc:
Swapping columns before rotation is the same as swapping the reversed columns after
rotation.
decls.statement:
theorem swapColumns_rotate (a b : Fin n) :
    (G.swapColumns a b).rotate = G.rotate.swapColumns a.rev b.rev

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.swapMarkings_rotate
decls.doc: Exchanging the two marking states commutes with the half-turn rotation.
decls.statement: theorem swapMarkings_rotate : G.swapMarkings.rotate = G.rotate.swapMarkings

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedRectangles_eq_all_of_le_two
decls.doc:
In grid size at most two, the fully blocked rectangles are exactly all oriented rectangles:
all rectangle interiors are empty, so emptiness and marking avoidance impose no extra condition.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedRectangles_eq_all_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (x y : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedRectangles x y = GridRectangleBetween.all x y

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedRectangleCount_eq_zero_of_le_two
decls.doc:
Every fully blocked rectangle coefficient vanishes in grid size at most two. If there are no
rectangles the count is zero; otherwise there are exactly two oriented rectangles, which cancel
over `ZMod 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedRectangleCount_eq_zero_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (x y : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedRectangleCount x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedRectangleCount_eq_zero_of_two
decls.doc: Every fully blocked rectangle coefficient vanishes on every `2 × 2` grid.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedRectangleCount_eq_zero_of_two
    (G : GridDiagram 2) (x y : GridState 2) :
    G.fullyBlockedRectangleCount x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero_of_le_two
decls.doc: The fully blocked differential of one generator vanishes in grid size at most two.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero_of_le_two
    (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero_of_two
decls.doc: The fully blocked differential of one generator vanishes on every `2 × 2` grid.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero_of_two
    (G : GridDiagram 2) (x : GridState 2) :
    G.fullyBlockedDifferentialOnGenerator x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedDifferential_eq_zero_of_le_two
decls.doc: The fully blocked differential is zero on every chain in grid size at most two.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedDifferential_eq_zero_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) :
    G.fullyBlockedDifferential = (0 : GridChain (ZMod 2) n →ₗ[ZMod 2] GridChain (ZMod 2) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedDifferential_eq_zero_of_two
decls.doc:
The fully blocked differential is zero on every `2 × 2` grid. This is the first
nontrivial cancellation sanity check for the rectangle-count definition.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedDifferential_eq_zero_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) :
    G.fullyBlockedDifferential =
      (0 : GridChain (ZMod 2) 2 →ₗ[ZMod 2] GridChain (ZMod 2) 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_OSet
decls.doc: The standard two-by-two diagram has `O` markings at `(0,0)` and `(1,1)`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwo_OSet :
    twoByTwo.OSet = {(0, 0), (1, 1)}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_XSet
decls.doc: The standard two-by-two diagram has `X` markings at `(0,1)` and `(1,0)`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwo_XSet :
    twoByTwo.XSet = {(0, 1), (1, 0)}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwoId_pairCard_self
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwoId_pairCard_self :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      p.1 < p.2 ∧ GridState.twoByTwoId p.1 < GridState.twoByTwoId p.2).card = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwoSwap_pairCard_self
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwoSwap_pairCard_self :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      p.1 < p.2 ∧ GridState.twoByTwoSwap p.1 < GridState.twoByTwoSwap p.2).card = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwoId_pairCard_swap
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwoId_pairCard_swap :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      p.1 < p.2 ∧ GridState.twoByTwoId p.1 < GridState.twoByTwoSwap p.2).card = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwoSwap_pairCard_id
decls.statement:
theorem twoByTwoSwap_pairCard_id :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 2 × Fin 2 =>
      p.1 < p.2 ∧ GridState.twoByTwoSwap p.1 < GridState.twoByTwoId p.2).card = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovXℤ_O_of_two
decls.doc: In a `2 × 2` diagram, the integer `X`-Maslov grading of the `O`-marking state is `2`.
decls.statement: theorem maslovXℤ_O_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.maslovXℤ G.O = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovOℤ_X_of_two
decls.doc: In a `2 × 2` diagram, the integer `O`-Maslov grading of the `X`-marking state is `2`.
decls.statement: theorem maslovOℤ_X_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.maslovOℤ G.X = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_O_of_two
decls.doc: Twice the Alexander grading of the `O`-marking state in a `2 × 2` diagram is `-2`.
decls.statement: theorem alexanderTwoℤ_O_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.alexanderTwoℤ G.O = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_X_of_two
decls.doc: Twice the Alexander grading of the `X`-marking state in a `2 × 2` diagram is `0`.
decls.statement: theorem alexanderTwoℤ_X_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.alexanderTwoℤ G.X = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_O_of_two
decls.doc: The Alexander grading of the `O`-marking state in a `2 × 2` diagram is `-1`.
decls.statement: theorem alexander_O_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.alexander G.O = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_X_of_two
decls.doc: The Alexander grading of the `X`-marking state in a `2 × 2` diagram is `0`.
decls.statement: theorem alexander_X_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) : G.alexander G.X = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovOℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId
decls.doc:
The integer `O`-Maslov grading of the identity generator in the standard two-by-two
diagram is `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem maslovOℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId :
    twoByTwo.maslovOℤ GridState.twoByTwoId = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovXℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId
decls.doc:
The integer `X`-Maslov grading of the identity generator in the standard two-by-two
diagram is `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem maslovXℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId :
    twoByTwo.maslovXℤ GridState.twoByTwoId = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId
decls.doc:
Twice the Alexander grading of the identity generator in the standard two-by-two diagram
is `-2`.
decls.statement:
theorem alexanderTwoℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId :
    twoByTwo.alexanderTwoℤ GridState.twoByTwoId = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId
decls.doc: The Alexander grading of the identity generator in the standard two-by-two diagram is `-1`.
decls.statement:
theorem alexander_twoByTwo_twoByTwoId :
    twoByTwo.alexander GridState.twoByTwoId = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovOℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc:
The integer `O`-Maslov grading of the transposition generator in the standard two-by-two
diagram is `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem maslovOℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap :
    twoByTwo.maslovOℤ GridState.twoByTwoSwap = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovXℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc:
The integer `X`-Maslov grading of the transposition generator in the standard two-by-two
diagram is `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem maslovXℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap :
    twoByTwo.maslovXℤ GridState.twoByTwoSwap = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc:
Twice the Alexander grading of the transposition generator in the standard two-by-two
diagram is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem alexanderTwoℤ_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap :
    twoByTwo.alexanderTwoℤ GridState.twoByTwoSwap = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc:
The Alexander grading of the transposition generator in the standard two-by-two diagram
is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem alexander_twoByTwo_twoByTwoSwap :
    twoByTwo.alexander GridState.twoByTwoSwap = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_eq_neg_one_or_eq_zero_of_two
decls.doc: Every generator of an arbitrary `2 × 2` diagram has Alexander grading `-1` or `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem alexander_eq_neg_one_or_eq_zero_of_two (G : GridDiagram 2) (x : GridState 2) :
    G.alexander x = -1 ∨ G.alexander x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_twoByTwo_eq_neg_one_or_eq_zero
decls.doc:
Every generator of the standard two-by-two diagram has one of the two computed Alexander
gradings.
decls.statement:
theorem alexander_twoByTwo_eq_neg_one_or_eq_zero (x : GridState 2) :
    twoByTwo.alexander x = -1 ∨ twoByTwo.alexander x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedCycleOfLeTwo
decls.doc:
The fully blocked cycle supported on a single grid state when the grid size is at most two.

The size hypothesis makes the fully blocked differential zero, so the singleton chain is a
cycle.
decls.statement:
def fullyBlockedCycleOfLeTwo (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedCycles

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedCycleOfLeTwo_coe
decls.doc: The chain underlying the small-grid cycle supported on `x` is the singleton chain at `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedCycleOfLeTwo_coe (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    (G.fullyBlockedCycleOfLeTwo hn x : GridChain (ZMod 2) n) = Finsupp.single x 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo
decls.doc: The fully blocked homology class represented by a single grid state in size at most two.
decls.statement:
def fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedHomology

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyEquivChainOfLeTwo_class
decls.doc:
Under the small-grid equivalence from homology to the chain module, the class represented by
`x` becomes the singleton chain at `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyEquivChainOfLeTwo_class (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedHomologyEquivChainOfLeTwo hn
        (G.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo hn x) =
      Finsupp.single x 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo
decls.doc:
The basis of fully blocked homology in grid size at most two, indexed by grid states.

It is obtained by transporting the standard singleton basis of the grid chain module through
the inverse of `fullyBlockedHomologyEquivChainOfLeTwo`.
decls.statement:
def fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo (hn : n ≤ 2) :
    Module.Basis (GridState n) (ZMod 2) G.fullyBlockedHomology

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_apply
decls.doc:
A vector of the small-grid homology basis is the class represented by its indexing grid
state.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_apply (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo hn x =
      G.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo hn x

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_repr_mk
decls.doc:
The coordinates of the class of a small-grid cycle are its chain coefficients.

Since the differential and the boundary submodule both vanish, passing to homology does not
change any coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_repr_mk (hn : n ≤ 2)
    (c : G.fullyBlockedCycles) :
    (G.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo hn).repr (Submodule.Quotient.mk c) =
      (c : GridChain (ZMod 2) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_repr_class
decls.doc:
The coordinate vector of the homology class represented by `x` is the singleton vector at
`x`.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo_repr_class (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    (G.fullyBlockedHomologyBasisOfLeTwo hn).repr
        (G.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo hn x) =
      Finsupp.single x 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo_ne_zero
decls.doc: Each single-state homology class is nonzero in grid size at most two.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo_ne_zero (hn : n ≤ 2) (x : GridState n) :
    G.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo hn x ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo_injective
decls.doc: Distinct grid states determine distinct fully blocked homology classes in size at most two.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo_injective (hn : n ≤ 2) :
    Function.Injective (G.fullyBlockedHomologyClassOfLeTwo hn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.insertPoint
decls.doc:
Insert a new point `(newColumn, newRow)` into a grid state.

Every old point `(c, x c)` is sent to
`(newColumn.succAbove c, newRow.succAbove (x c))`.
decls.statement: def insertPoint (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) : GridState (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.insertPoint_apply_newColumn
decls.doc: The inserted column contains the inserted row.
decls.statement:
theorem insertPoint_apply_newColumn (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) :
    x.insertPoint newColumn newRow newColumn = newRow

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.insertPoint_apply_succAbove
decls.doc: An old column contains the embedded image of its old row after inserting a point.
decls.statement:
theorem insertPoint_apply_succAbove (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (c : Fin n) :
    x.insertPoint newColumn newRow (newColumn.succAbove c) =
      newRow.succAbove (x c)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.splitPoint
decls.doc:
Split the point in column `splitColumn` across an inserted row and column.

The old point at `(splitColumn, x splitColumn)` is replaced by the two points
`(newColumn, newRow.succAbove (x splitColumn))` and
`(newColumn.succAbove splitColumn, newRow)`. All other old points are embedded as in
`GridState.insertPoint`.
decls.statement:
def splitPoint (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn : Fin n) : GridState (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.splitPoint_apply_newColumn
decls.doc: The new column of a split point contains the embedded old row of the split point.
decls.statement:
theorem splitPoint_apply_newColumn (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    x.splitPoint newColumn newRow splitColumn newColumn =
      newRow.succAbove (x splitColumn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.splitPoint_apply_splitColumn
decls.doc: The embedded old column of a split point contains the new row.
decls.statement:
theorem splitPoint_apply_splitColumn (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    x.splitPoint newColumn newRow splitColumn (newColumn.succAbove splitColumn) =
      newRow

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.splitPoint_apply_succAbove
decls.doc: Away from the split column, `splitPoint` embeds old points in the inserted grid.
decls.statement:
theorem splitPoint_apply_succAbove (x : GridState n) (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn c : Fin n) :
    x.splitPoint newColumn newRow splitColumn (newColumn.succAbove c) =
      if c = splitColumn then newRow else newRow.succAbove (x c)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeO
decls.doc:
Stabilize a grid diagram by splitting the `O`-marking in `splitColumn`.

The `O` state uses the two off-diagonal corners of the inserted row and column, while the new
`X`-marking occupies their intersection. The elementary-move predicate below separately requires
the inserted row and column to be adjacent to the split marking.
decls.statement:
def stabilizeO (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    GridDiagram (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeX
decls.doc:
Stabilize a grid diagram by splitting the `X`-marking in `splitColumn`.

The `X` state uses the two off-diagonal corners of the inserted row and column, while the new
`O`-marking occupies their intersection. The elementary-move predicate below separately requires
the inserted row and column to be adjacent to the split marking.
decls.statement:
def stabilizeX (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    GridDiagram (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeO_O
decls.doc: The `O` state of an `O`-stabilization is obtained by splitting the chosen `O`-marking.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeO_O (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeO newColumn newRow splitColumn).O =
      G.O.splitPoint newColumn newRow splitColumn

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeO_X
decls.doc: The `X` state of an `O`-stabilization is obtained by inserting the new `X`-marking.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeO_X (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeO newColumn newRow splitColumn).X =
      G.X.insertPoint newColumn newRow

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeX_O
decls.doc: The `O` state of an `X`-stabilization is obtained by inserting the new `O`-marking.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeX_O (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeX newColumn newRow splitColumn).O =
      G.O.insertPoint newColumn newRow

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeX_X
decls.doc: The `X` state of an `X`-stabilization is obtained by splitting the chosen `X`-marking.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeX_X (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeX newColumn newRow splitColumn).X =
      G.X.splitPoint newColumn newRow splitColumn

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeO_swapMarkings
decls.doc: Exchanging the marking types turns an `O`-stabilization into an `X`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeO_swapMarkings (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeO newColumn newRow splitColumn).swapMarkings =
      G.swapMarkings.stabilizeX newColumn newRow splitColumn

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.stabilizeX_swapMarkings
decls.doc: Exchanging the marking types turns an `X`-stabilization into an `O`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizeX_swapMarkings (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1)) (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    (G.stabilizeX newColumn newRow splitColumn).swapMarkings =
      G.swapMarkings.stabilizeO newColumn newRow splitColumn

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsOStabilization
decls.doc:
Two grid diagrams differ by an elementary stabilization that splits an `O`-marking.

The new column is cyclically adjacent to the embedded split column, and the new row is cyclically
adjacent to the embedded row of its `O`-marking. The two disjunctions independently choose the
cyclic orientation, giving the four `O`-stabilization corner types.
decls.statement: def IsOStabilization (G : GridDiagram n) (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isOStabilization_stabilizeO
decls.doc: A local `O`-stabilization construction is an elementary `O`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem isOStabilization_stabilizeO (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn : Fin n)
    (hColumn : finRotate (n + 1) newColumn = newColumn.succAbove splitColumn ∨
      finRotate (n + 1) (newColumn.succAbove splitColumn) = newColumn)
    (hRow : finRotate (n + 1) newRow = newRow.succAbove (G.O splitColumn) ∨
      finRotate (n + 1) (newRow.succAbove (G.O splitColumn)) = newRow) :
    IsOStabilization G (G.stabilizeO newColumn newRow splitColumn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isOStabilization_stabilizeO_castSucc
decls.doc:
Inserting a column immediately before `splitColumn` and a row immediately before its
`O`-marking gives an elementary `O`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem isOStabilization_stabilizeO_castSucc (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    IsOStabilization G
      (G.stabilizeO splitColumn.castSucc (G.O splitColumn).castSucc splitColumn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsXStabilization
decls.doc:
Two grid diagrams differ by an elementary stabilization that splits an `X`-marking.

The new column is cyclically adjacent to the embedded split column, and the new row is cyclically
adjacent to the embedded row of its `X`-marking. The two disjunctions independently choose the
cyclic orientation, giving the four `X`-stabilization corner types.
decls.statement: def IsXStabilization (G : GridDiagram n) (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isXStabilization_stabilizeX
decls.doc: A local `X`-stabilization construction is an elementary `X`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem isXStabilization_stabilizeX (newColumn newRow : Fin (n + 1))
    (splitColumn : Fin n)
    (hColumn : finRotate (n + 1) newColumn = newColumn.succAbove splitColumn ∨
      finRotate (n + 1) (newColumn.succAbove splitColumn) = newColumn)
    (hRow : finRotate (n + 1) newRow = newRow.succAbove (G.X splitColumn) ∨
      finRotate (n + 1) (newRow.succAbove (G.X splitColumn)) = newRow) :
    IsXStabilization G (G.stabilizeX newColumn newRow splitColumn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isXStabilization_stabilizeX_castSucc
decls.doc:
Inserting a column immediately before `splitColumn` and a row immediately before its
`X`-marking gives an elementary `X`-stabilization.
decls.statement:
theorem isXStabilization_stabilizeX_castSucc (splitColumn : Fin n) :
    IsXStabilization G
      (G.stabilizeX splitColumn.castSucc (G.X splitColumn).castSucc splitColumn)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isOStabilization_swapMarkings
decls.doc:
Exchanging the marking types turns an `O`-stabilization relation into an
`X`-stabilization relation.
decls.statement:
theorem isOStabilization_swapMarkings (G : GridDiagram n)
    (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) :
    IsOStabilization G.swapMarkings G'.swapMarkings ↔ IsXStabilization G G'

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isXStabilization_swapMarkings
decls.doc:
Exchanging the marking types turns an `X`-stabilization relation into an
`O`-stabilization relation.
decls.statement:
theorem isXStabilization_swapMarkings (G : GridDiagram n)
    (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) :
    IsXStabilization G.swapMarkings G'.swapMarkings ↔ IsOStabilization G G'

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsStabilization
decls.doc: One elementary grid stabilization, splitting either an `O`- or an `X`-marking.
decls.statement: def IsStabilization (G : GridDiagram n) (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isStabilization_swapMarkings
decls.doc: Exchanging the marking types preserves the elementary stabilization relation.
decls.statement:
theorem isStabilization_swapMarkings (G : GridDiagram n)
    (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) :
    IsStabilization G.swapMarkings G'.swapMarkings ↔ IsStabilization G G'

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsDestabilization
decls.doc: One elementary grid destabilization, oriented from the larger diagram to the smaller one.
decls.statement: def IsDestabilization (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1)) (G : GridDiagram n) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isDestabilization_swapMarkings
decls.doc: Exchanging the marking types preserves the elementary destabilization relation.
decls.statement:
theorem isDestabilization_swapMarkings (G' : GridDiagram (n + 1))
    (G : GridDiagram n) :
    IsDestabilization G'.swapMarkings G.swapMarkings ↔ IsDestabilization G' G

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card
decls.doc: The number of grid states on an `n × n` grid is `n!`.
decls.statement: theorem card (n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (GridState n) = n.factorial

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card_univ
decls.doc: The universe finite set of grid states has cardinality `n!`.
decls.statement: theorem card_univ (n : ℕ) : (Finset.univ : Finset (GridState n)).card = n.factorial

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.natCard
decls.doc: The natural cardinality of grid states is `n!`.
decls.statement: theorem natCard (n : ℕ) : Nat.card (GridState n) = n.factorial

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card_zero
decls.doc: There is one grid state on the empty grid.
decls.statement: theorem card_zero : Fintype.card (GridState 0) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card_one
decls.doc: There is one grid state on a `1 × 1` grid.
decls.statement: theorem card_one : Fintype.card (GridState 1) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.card_two
decls.doc: There are two grid states on a `2 × 2` grid.
decls.statement: theorem card_two : Fintype.card (GridState 2) = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.subsingletonOfLeOne
decls.doc: Any two grid states are equal whenever the grid has at most one row and column.
decls.statement: theorem subsingletonOfLeOne (hn : n ≤ 1) : Subsingleton (GridState n)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.instUniqueZero
decls.doc: There is a unique grid state on the empty grid.
decls.statement: instance instUniqueZero : Unique (GridState 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.default_zero_eq
decls.doc: The unique empty-grid state is the state associated to the identity permutation.
decls.statement: theorem default_zero_eq : (default : GridState 0) = (equivPerm 0).symm 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.instUniqueOne
decls.doc: There is a unique grid state on a `1 × 1` grid.
decls.statement: instance instUniqueOne : Unique (GridState 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.apply_eq_zero
decls.doc: The unique `1 × 1` grid state sends the only column to the only row.
decls.statement: theorem apply_eq_zero (x : GridState 1) (c : Fin 1) : x c = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.eq_equivPerm_symm_one_or_eq_equivPerm_symm_swap
decls.doc: The two grid states on a `2 × 2` grid are exactly the identity and the transposition.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_equivPerm_symm_one_or_eq_equivPerm_symm_swap (x : GridState 2) :
    x = (equivPerm 2).symm 1 ∨ x = (equivPerm 2).symm (Equiv.swap 0 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoId
decls.doc: The identity grid state on a `2 × 2` grid.
decls.statement: abbrev twoByTwoId : GridState 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc: The transposition grid state on a `2 × 2` grid.
decls.statement: abbrev twoByTwoSwap : GridState 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoId_zero
decls.doc: The identity two-by-two state sends column `0` to row `0`.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwoId_zero : twoByTwoId 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoId_one
decls.doc: The identity two-by-two state sends column `1` to row `1`.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwoId_one : twoByTwoId 1 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoSwap_zero
decls.doc: The transposition two-by-two state sends column `0` to row `1`.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwoSwap_zero : twoByTwoSwap 0 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoSwap_one
decls.doc: The transposition two-by-two state sends column `1` to row `0`.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwoSwap_one : twoByTwoSwap 1 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoId_ne_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc: The two named `2 × 2` grid states are distinct.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwoId_ne_twoByTwoSwap : twoByTwoId ≠ twoByTwoSwap

decls.name: TauCeti.GridState.eq_twoByTwoId_or_eq_twoByTwoSwap
decls.doc: Every `2 × 2` grid state is either the identity state or the transposition state.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_twoByTwoId_or_eq_twoByTwoSwap (x : GridState 2) :
    x = twoByTwoId ∨ x = twoByTwoSwap

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isCycle_finRotate_torus
decls.doc: The cyclic shift of the columns of a torus link grid is a cycle.
decls.statement: theorem isCycle_finRotate_torus : (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1))).IsCycle

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.support_finRotate_torus
decls.doc: The cyclic shift of the columns of a torus link grid moves every column.
decls.statement:
theorem support_finRotate_torus :
    (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1))).support = Finset.univ

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_support_finRotate_torus
decls.doc: The cyclic shift of the columns of a torus link grid is a cycle of length the grid number.
decls.statement:
theorem card_support_finRotate_torus :
    (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1))).support.card = p + 1 + (q + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.not_card_dvd_torus
decls.doc:
The shift `q + 1` of the `X` markings of a torus link grid is not a multiple of the grid
number, which is what makes the shifted diagonal disjoint from the diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem not_card_dvd_torus :
    ¬(finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1))).support.card ∣ q + 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink
decls.doc:
The standard grid diagram of the `(p + 1, q + 1)` torus link, of grid number
`(p + 1) + (q + 1)`.

The `O` markings occupy the diagonal squares and the `X` markings the diagonal shifted up by
`q + 1` rows. Following the markings alternately horizontally and vertically traverses staircases
that wind `q + 1` times around the torus in one direction and `p + 1` times in the other.
decls.statement: def torusLink : GridDiagram (p + 1 + (q + 1))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink_O_toPerm
decls.doc: The `O` markings of a standard torus link grid are the identity permutation graph.
decls.statement: theorem torusLink_O_toPerm : (torusLink p q).O.toPerm = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink_X_toPerm
decls.doc:
The `X` markings of a standard torus link grid are the `(q + 1)`-st power of the cyclic shift
permutation graph.
decls.statement:
theorem torusLink_X_toPerm :
    (torusLink p q).X.toPerm = finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1)) ^ (q + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink_O_apply
decls.doc: The `O` marking of a standard torus link grid in a column is in the diagonal row.
decls.statement: theorem torusLink_O_apply (c : Fin (p + 1 + (q + 1))) : (torusLink p q).O c = c

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink_X_apply
decls.doc:
The `X` marking of a standard torus link grid in a column is `q + 1` rows above the
diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem torusLink_X_apply (c : Fin (p + 1 + (q + 1))) :
    (torusLink p q).X c = (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1)) ^ (q + 1)) c

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.torusLink_zero_right
decls.doc:
With `q = 0` the standard torus link grid is the standard unknot grid: the `(p + 1, 1)` torus
link is the unknot.
decls.statement: theorem torusLink_zero_right : torusLink p 0 = unknot p

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.relabelRows_relabelColumns_torusLink
decls.doc:
A standard torus link grid is invariant under shifting all rows and all columns by one at the
same time: the shift commutes with its own power.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelRows_relabelColumns_torusLink :
    ((torusLink p q).relabelRows (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1)))).relabelColumns
        (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1))) = torusLink p q

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentPerm_torusLink
decls.doc:
Traversing a standard torus link grid from an `O` marking to the `X` marking in its row and
back down to the next `O` marking shifts the column down by `q + 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem componentPerm_torusLink :
    (torusLink p q).componentPerm = (finRotate (p + 1 + (q + 1)) ^ (q + 1))⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.gcd_torus
decls.doc:
Cancelling the shift out of the grid number inside a greatest common divisor:
`gcd ((p + 1) + (q + 1)) (q + 1) = gcd (p + 1) (q + 1)`.
decls.statement: theorem gcd_torus : (p + 1 + (q + 1)).gcd (q + 1) = (p + 1).gcd (q + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentCycleType_torusLink
decls.doc:
The components of a standard torus link grid all carry the same number of markings, and there
are `gcd (p + 1) (q + 1)` of them: exactly the number of components of the `(p + 1, q + 1)` torus
link.
decls.statement:
theorem componentCycleType_torusLink :
    (torusLink p q).componentCycleType =
      Multiset.replicate ((p + 1).gcd (q + 1))
        ((p + 1 + (q + 1)) / (p + 1).gcd (q + 1))

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentCount_torusLink
decls.doc: A standard torus link grid represents a link with `gcd (p + 1) (q + 1)` components.
decls.statement:
theorem componentCount_torusLink :
    (torusLink p q).componentCount = (p + 1).gcd (q + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isKnot_torusLink_iff
decls.doc:
A standard torus link grid represents a knot exactly when its two winding numbers are
coprime.
decls.statement: theorem isKnot_torusLink_iff : (torusLink p q).IsKnot ↔ (p + 1).Coprime (q + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isKnot_torusLink_one_two
decls.doc:
The `5 × 5` grid diagram `torusLink 1 2` of the `(2, 3)` torus knot, the trefoil, represents a
knot.
decls.statement: theorem isKnot_torusLink_one_two : (torusLink 1 2).IsKnot

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentCount_torusLink_one_one
decls.doc:
The `4 × 4` grid diagram `torusLink 1 1` of the `(2, 2)` torus link, the Hopf link, represents
a two-component link.
decls.statement: theorem componentCount_torusLink_one_one : (torusLink 1 1).componentCount = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.not_isKnot_torusLink_one_one
decls.doc:
The `4 × 4` Hopf link grid does not represent a knot, so the family really does produce
links of more than one component.
decls.statement: theorem not_isKnot_torusLink_one_one : ¬(torusLink 1 1).IsKnot

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentCycleType_torusLink_two_two
decls.doc:
The `6 × 6` grid diagram `torusLink 2 2` of the `(3, 3)` torus link has three components, each
carrying two of its six markings.
decls.statement:
theorem componentCycleType_torusLink_two_two :
    (torusLink 2 2).componentCycleType = {2, 2, 2}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot
decls.doc:
The standard grid diagram for the unknot with grid number `n + 2`.

The `O` markings occupy the diagonal squares and the `X` markings the diagonal shifted up by one
row. Following the markings alternately horizontally and vertically traverses a single staircase
that winds once around the torus in each direction, so the represented link is the unknot.
decls.statement: def unknot (n : ℕ) : GridDiagram (n + 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_O_toPerm
decls.doc: The `O` markings of the standard unknot grid are the identity permutation graph.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_O_toPerm : (unknot n).O.toPerm = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_X_toPerm
decls.doc: The `X` markings of the standard unknot grid are the cyclic shift permutation graph.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_X_toPerm : (unknot n).X.toPerm = finRotate (n + 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_O_apply
decls.doc: The `O` marking of the standard unknot grid in a column is in the diagonal row.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_O_apply (c : Fin (n + 2)) : (unknot n).O c = c

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_X_apply
decls.doc: The `X` marking of the standard unknot grid in a column is one row above the diagonal.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_X_apply (c : Fin (n + 2)) : (unknot n).X c = finRotate (n + 2) c

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_X_apply_eq_add_one
decls.doc: The `X` markings of the standard unknot grid form the shifted diagonal.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_X_apply_eq_add_one (c : Fin (n + 2)) : (unknot n).X c = c + 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo
decls.doc:
The standard `2 × 2` grid diagram with `O` markings on the identity state and `X`
markings on the transposition state. This is the usual smallest grid diagram for the unknot.
decls.statement: abbrev twoByTwo : GridDiagram 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_O
decls.doc: The `O`-marking state of the standard two-by-two diagram is the identity state.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwo_O : twoByTwo.O = GridState.twoByTwoId

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X
decls.doc: The `X`-marking state of the standard two-by-two diagram is the transposition state.
decls.statement: theorem twoByTwo_X : twoByTwo.X = GridState.twoByTwoSwap

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.unknot_zero
decls.doc: In grid number two the standard unknot grid is the `2 × 2` diagram `twoByTwo`.
decls.statement: theorem unknot_zero : unknot 0 = twoByTwo

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentPerm_unknot
decls.doc:
Traversing the standard unknot grid from an `O` marking to the `X` marking in its row and
back down to the next `O` marking shifts the column down by one.
decls.statement: theorem componentPerm_unknot : (unknot n).componentPerm = (finRotate (n + 2))⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isKnot_unknot
decls.doc:
The standard unknot grid diagram represents a knot: its component permutation is a single
cycle through all `n + 2` markings.
decls.statement: theorem isKnot_unknot : (unknot n).IsKnot

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.componentCycleType_unknot
decls.doc: The sole component of the standard unknot grid diagram carries all `n + 2` markings.
decls.statement: theorem componentCycleType_unknot : (unknot n).componentCycleType = {n + 2}

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.relabelRows_relabelColumns_unknot
decls.doc:
The standard unknot grid diagram is invariant under shifting all rows and all columns by one
at the same time.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelRows_relabelColumns_unknot :
    ((unknot n).relabelRows (finRotate (n + 2))).relabelColumns (finRotate (n + 2)) = unknot n

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_lt_split
decls.doc: Splitting the pairs of columns in increasing order according to an auxiliary predicate.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_lt_split (P : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2 ∧ P p).card
        + (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2 ∧ ¬ P p).card
      = (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_graph
decls.doc:
A set of column pairs cut out by prescribing the second column as a function of the first,
which is required to avoid the last column, has `n + 1` elements.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_graph (f : Fin (n + 2) → Fin (n + 2)) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) =>
        p.1 ≠ Fin.last (n + 1) ∧ p.2 = f p.1).card = n + 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_lt_O_lt_O
decls.doc:
The number of increasing column pairs is unchanged by additionally demanding that the two
diagonal `O` markings be in increasing order, which they always are.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_lt_O_lt_O :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) =>
        p.1 < p.2 ∧ (unknot n).O p.1 < (unknot n).O p.2).card
      = (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_lt_O_lt_X
decls.doc:
Among the increasing column pairs, exactly the `n + 1` pairs ending in the last column fail to
put the first diagonal `O` marking below the second shifted `X` marking.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_lt_O_lt_X :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) =>
        p.1 < p.2 ∧ (unknot n).O p.1 < (unknot n).X p.2).card + (n + 1)
      = (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_lt_X_lt_O
decls.doc:
Among the increasing column pairs, exactly the `n + 1` pairs of consecutive columns fail to
put the first shifted `X` marking below the second diagonal `O` marking.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_lt_X_lt_O :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) =>
        p.1 < p.2 ∧ (unknot n).X p.1 < (unknot n).O p.2).card + (n + 1)
      = (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.card_filter_lt_X_lt_X
decls.doc:
Among the increasing column pairs, exactly the `n + 1` pairs ending in the last column fail to
keep the two shifted `X` markings in increasing order.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_lt_X_lt_X :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) =>
        p.1 < p.2 ∧ (unknot n).X p.1 < (unknot n).X p.2).card + (n + 1)
      = (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin (n + 2) × Fin (n + 2) => p.1 < p.2).card

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovXℤ_unknot_O
decls.doc:
The `X`-Maslov grading of the `O`-marking state of the standard unknot grid is the grid
number.
decls.statement: theorem maslovXℤ_unknot_O : (unknot n).maslovXℤ (unknot n).O = n + 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.maslovOℤ_unknot_X
decls.doc:
The `O`-Maslov grading of the `X`-marking state of the standard unknot grid is the grid
number. Swapping the roles of the two marking states turns the count computed in
`maslovXℤ_unknot_O` into this one, so no column-pair count has to be redone.
decls.statement: theorem maslovOℤ_unknot_X : (unknot n).maslovOℤ (unknot n).X = n + 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_unknot_X
decls.doc: Twice the Alexander grading of the `X`-marking state of the standard unknot grid vanishes.
decls.statement: theorem alexanderTwoℤ_unknot_X : (unknot n).alexanderTwoℤ (unknot n).X = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexanderTwoℤ_unknot_O
decls.doc:
Twice the Alexander grading of the `O`-marking state of the standard unknot grid is
`-2 (n + 1)`.
decls.statement: theorem alexanderTwoℤ_unknot_O : (unknot n).alexanderTwoℤ (unknot n).O = -2 * (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_unknot_X
decls.doc: The Alexander grading of the `X`-marking state of the standard unknot grid is zero.
decls.statement: theorem alexander_unknot_X : (unknot n).alexander (unknot n).X = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_unknot_O
decls.doc:
The Alexander grading of the `O`-marking state of the standard unknot grid is `-(n + 1)`,
one less than the negated grid number.
decls.statement: theorem alexander_unknot_O : (unknot n).alexander (unknot n).O = -(n + 1)
